## 2.2
```{r}
library(vars)

# Calculate lag selection criteria (maximum 12 lags)
lag_selection <- VARselect(data_var_ts,
                           lag.max = 12,
                           type = "const")

# Display AIC and BIC for all lag lengths
lag_selection$criteria[c("AIC(n)", "SC(n)"), ]

# Display optimal lag according to AIC and BIC
lag_selection$selection[c("AIC(n)", "SC(n)")]
```
```{r}
# Display HQ and FPE for all lag lengths
lag_selection$criteria[c("HQ(n)", "FPE(n)"), ]

# Display optimal lag according to HQ and FPE
lag_selection$selection[c("HQ(n)", "FPE(n)")]
```

## 2.6
```{r}
# Extract reduced-form residuals
var_residuals <- residuals(var_model)
# Calculate their covariance matrix
Sigma_e <- cov(var_residuals)
# Display the matrix
round(Sigma_e, 4)
```
```{r}
# Calculate the lower-triangular Cholesky factor
P <- t(chol(Sigma_e))
# Display the result
round(P, 4)
```
```{r}
# Extract reduced-form residuals
var_residuals <- residuals(var_model)

# Calculate their covariance matrix
Sigma_e <- cov(var_residuals)

# Display the matrix
round(Sigma_e, 4)

# Calculate the lower-triangular Cholesky factor
P <- t(chol(Sigma_e))

# Display the result
round(P, 4)
```
```{r}
# QUESTION 2.6 – Structural identification using Cholesky decomposition

# 1. Extract the residual covariance matrix from the estimated VAR
Sigma_e <- summary(var_model)$covres

# Display the residual covariance matrix
round(Sigma_e, 4)


# 2. Calculate the lower-triangular Cholesky impact matrix
P <- t(chol(Sigma_e))

# Display the Cholesky matrix
round(P, 4)


# 3. Calculate the matrix of contemporaneous links
B0 <- solve(P)

# Display B0
round(B0, 4)


# 4. Normalize B0 to have ones on the diagonal
B0_normalized <- diag(1 / diag(B0)) %*% B0

# Display normalized B0
round(B0_normalized, 4)
```

## 2.7
```{r}
# Ensure variable names are accessible
var_names <- colnames(data_var_ts)

# Compute IRFs for inflation (y1) and GDP growth (y2) following a shock to monetary policy (y3)
irf_chol <- irf(
  var_model,
  impulse = var_names[3],          # y3: Monetary policy surprises
  response = c(var_names[1], var_names[2]), # y1: Inflation, y2: GDP growth
  n.ahead = 24,                    # 24-month horizon
  ortho = TRUE,                    # Use Cholesky orthogonalization
  boot = TRUE,                     # Bootstrap for confidence intervals
  runs = 1000,                     # Number of bootstrap replications
  seed = 123                       # Set seed for reproducibility
)

# Save both impulse response plots as one image
png("IRF_Q2_7.png", width = 1200, height = 900, res = 120)

plot(irf_chol,
     plot.type = "multiple",
     nc = 1,
     mar.multi = c(3, 4, 2, 1),
     oma.multi = c(3, 3, 3, 1),
     main = "Responses to a Contractionary Monetary Policy Shock")

dev.off()
getwd()
```

## 2.9
```{r}
library(svars)

# Estimate the GARCH-identified SVAR
set.seed(123)
svar_garch <- id.garch(var_model)

# Display estimation and identification results
summary(svar_garch)
```

## 2.10
```{r}
# Question 2.10 – GARCH impulse response functions

# Identify the shock with the largest impact on monetary policy surprises
mp_col <- which.max(abs(svar_garch$B["y3", ]))

# Copy the GARCH model
svar_mp <- svar_garch

# Normalize the monetary policy shock to represent contractionary policy
if (svar_mp$B["y3", mp_col] < 0) {
  svar_mp$B[, mp_col] <- -svar_mp$B[, mp_col]
}

# Calculate impulse responses over months 0–24
irf_garch <- vars::irf(svar_mp, n.ahead = 25)

# Save the inflation and GDP growth responses
png("IRF_GARCH_Q2_10.png", width = 1200, height = 800, res = 120)

print(plot(irf_garch,
           selection = list(mp_col, c(1, 2)),
           scales = "free_y"))

dev.off()
```
```{r}
# Question 2.10 – Correct GARCH impulse response plots

png("IRF_GARCH_Q2_10_corrected.png",
    width = 1200, height = 800, res = 120)

print(plot(
  irf_garch,
  selection = list(c(1, 2), mp_col),
  scales = "free_y"
))

dev.off()
```

## 3.1 (pre)
```{r}
# Load the dataset
load("data_vec.RData")

# Examine the structure of the dataset
str(data_vec)

# Display the first and last observations
head(data_vec)
tail(data_vec)

# Check the number of observations and variables
dim(data_vec)
```
```{r}
# Declare the data as monthly time series
data_vec_ts <- ts(data_vec,
                  start = c(1972, 1),
                  frequency = 12)

# Verify the time-series structure
start(data_vec_ts)
end(data_vec_ts)
frequency(data_vec_ts)

# Plot all three variables

     main = "Yield Curve Factors and Industrial Production",
     xlab = "Year")
```
## 3.1
```{r}
# ADF test for the level factor (with drift)
adf_L <- ur.df(data_vec_ts[, "L"],
               type = "drift",
               lags = 12,
               selectlags = "BIC")

# ADF test for the slope factor (with drift)
adf_S <- ur.df(data_vec_ts[, "S"],
               type = "drift",
               lags = 12,
               selectlags = "BIC")

# ADF test for industrial production (with trend)
adf_IP <- ur.df(data_vec_ts[, "IP"],
                type = "trend",
                lags = 12,
                selectlags = "BIC")

# Display the results
summary(adf_IP)
```
```{r}
summary(adf_L)
summary(adf_S)
```
```{r}
# KPSS test for the level factor
kpss_L <- ur.kpss(data_vec_ts[, "L"],
                  type = "mu",
                  lags = "short")

# KPSS test for the slope factor
kpss_S <- ur.kpss(data_vec_ts[, "S"],
                  type = "mu",
                  lags = "short")

# KPSS test for industrial production
kpss_IP <- ur.kpss(data_vec_ts[, "IP"],
                   type = "tau",
                   lags = "short")

# Display results
summary(kpss_L)
summary(kpss_S)
summary(kpss_IP)
```
```{r}

                lags = 12,

adf_dIP <- ur.df(data_vec_diff[, "IP"],
                 type = "drift",
                 lags = 12,
                 selectlags = "BIC")

summary(adf_dL)
summary(adf_dS)
summary(adf_dIP)
```

## 3.2
```{r}
# Load package
library(vars)

# Select VAR lag length
lag_selection <- VARselect(data_vec_ts,
                           lag.max = 12,
                           type = "const")

# Display selected lag lengths
lag_selection$selection

# Display information criteria
lag_selection$criteria
```

```{r}
# Johansen trace test
johansen_trace <- ca.jo(data_vec_ts,
                        type = "trace",
                        ecdet = "const",
                        K = 4,
                        spec = "longrun")

# Display results
summary(johansen_trace)
```

```{r}
# Johansen maximum eigenvalue test
johansen_eigen <- ca.jo(data_vec_ts,
                        type = "eigen",
                        ecdet = "const",
                        K = 4,
                        spec = "longrun")

# Display results
summary(johansen_eigen)
```
```{r}
# Estimate the restricted VEC model with rank 1
vec_estimates <- cajorls(johansen_trace, r = 1)

# Display the estimated cointegrating vector
vec_estimates$beta

# Display the VEC model coefficients
summary(vec_estimates$rlm)
```
